evals.prompt: I have an Umbraco 17 site. Create a custom dashboard Health Check that verifies Umbraco:CMS:Global:UseHttps is true in production, places it in the Security group, and gives editors a useful official documentation link. Tell me how to verify it in Settings > Health Check.
evals.expected_output: The agent chooses the backend C# surface, fetches the official Health Check documentation, implements the appropriate configuration-check API for Umbraco 17, and explains dashboard verification.
expectations: The response distinguishes a backoffice Health Check from a health probe endpoint
The implementation uses a stable HealthCheck attribute with a unique GUID, concise name, description, and Security group
The check reads Umbraco:CMS:Global:UseHttps and treats true as the recommended accepted value
The response links to the official .md Health Check documentation and gives Settings > Health Check verification steps
If a buildable project exists, the agent reports a successful build only after running it; otherwise it explicitly says build verification was unavailable

evals.prompt: Add a custom Umbraco 17 Health Check that checks whether robots.txt exists and offers a safe action to create it when missing. Use localized messages and explain how the check can be scheduled and notified.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the general backend C# surface, separates status checking from remediation and notification configuration, and handles failures explicitly.
expectations: The implementation derives from the current Umbraco HealthCheck API and returns an explicit success or error status
A remediation action is offered only when the file is missing, has a stable alias, and is validated in ExecuteAction
Write failures are surfaced as an error and logged rather than swallowed or reported as success
User-facing messages use the project localization mechanism, and the response links to official Health Check and health-check configuration documentation
The response explains that scheduled execution/notifications are separate from dashboard loading
Build verification is reported honestly

evals.prompt: On our Umbraco 17 Razor site, show a localized health-check warning to visitors. We support English, Danish, and German, use Dictionary items, and need a safe fallback if the translation is missing.
evals.expected_output: The agent chooses the Razor surface, keeps health status computation in backend code, organises stable Dictionary aliases by feature/message, renders the selected culture safely, and defines an explicit fallback chain.
expectations: The response explicitly chooses Razor only because frontend presentation was requested and keeps the check logic out of the view
Dictionary aliases are stable and organised by feature and message purpose rather than translated names
English, Danish, and German values are treated as deliberate supported cultures
The fallback order is explicit and ends in a safe non-sensitive invariant message or failure state
Razor output is encoded and does not expose configuration secrets
Build verification is reported honestly

evals.prompt: I need a Kubernetes readiness endpoint for an Umbraco 17 deployment, not a Settings dashboard check.
evals.expected_output: The agent skips this skill and directs the user to the official Health Probes documentation.
expectations: The response does not create a custom HealthCheck class or Dictionary setup
The response identifies readiness/liveness probes as outside this skill’s scope
The response links to the official .md Health Probes documentation
